output.summary: Adds engine/legacy.py: free local signals (old-format POLICY.json, PROJECT_AUDIT/BOOTSTRAP/rules files, old ignore blocks, cleanup_legacy's retired install roots) plus, only when a cached key of (engine version, remote, signals) changes, one ls-remote for old ref namespaces and one gh GraphQL search for open legacy-labelled or envelope-marked issues, cached in <git-common>/zzzops/legacy.json; validate always re-checks so migration is detected, not remembered. `next`/`validate` gain a top-level `legacy` item with counts and the new shipped skill `migrate-zzzops-repository` (a triage checklist with this repo's 115-issue audit as its worked example); an old-format policy becomes the `legacy_policy` blocker (exit 4) naming that skill; dismissal is an optional `settings.legacy.ignore`. It restores R11's lost version-keyed detection without its gate, and amends DESIGN §10 item 10 with one bounded GitHub-call exception.

findings.text: F1: The contract amendment covers only §10 item 10. §10 item 2 binds to the §3.15 counts (next = 1 fetch, 0 GitHub), and a cache miss adds 1 ls-remote and 1 gh; validate always pays both. The existing CostBudgetTests (next == (1,0,['fetch']); journeys: exactly one trace line) run on a cold cache and would fail, and the 'filter on pr calls' option would hollow out the no-GitHub guard. Fix: amend the §3.15 next row and add a validate row; seed a matching clean cache with legacy's key function and keep the totals assertions unchanged (no filtering, no off switch); add a cold-cache budget test of exactly fetch+ls-remote and 1 api graphql; say where the DESIGN.md amendment is recorded (it is not in the repo).

F2: Any gh failure is cached as 'unavailable' until the key changes. With no local signals (the policy already bootstrapped but old issues still open, a half-migrated repo), one transient 502, timeout or rate limit on the first next hides all legacy issues in that clone until the engine version changes. Fix: cache only permanent failures (not installed, not authenticated); for GhError.transient store a retry_after (e.g. 24 h), and extend test 8 to cover both cases.

F3: The migrate skill is not usable by an agent new to ZzzOps. (a) The triage classes and OBSOLETE comments depend on 'DESIGN §5 R1-R15', which is not shipped (DESIGN.md is not in the plugin or repo, and MIGRATING.md has no removal list): ship a self-contained removal table (old feature/label family -> R id -> replacement or removed) in the skill references. (b) The inventory (gh issue list --label zzzops plus an unspecified marker search) differs from the detector's set (zzzops OR zzzops:schema:v1/v2, marker on unlabelled issues, minus linked), so the item may never disappear after triage: have validate's legacy output include the counted issue numbers (already cached, first 100) or the exact queries, and give exact gh commands that use the same query. (c) The MIGRATING.md carry-forward uses the tag zzzops-pre-reset, which exists only in the ZzzOps repo: say to clone david-rzepa/zzzops at that tag.

output.summary: Sound approach: bounded R11-style version detection, the right disclosure shape, and an old-format policy blocker. Three changes needed: (F1) amend DESIGN §3.15 next/validate counts as well as §10 item 10, and keep cost tests strict by seeding the cache rather than filtering, plus a cold-cache budget test; (F2) do not cache transient gh failures for the whole engine version; (F3) make the migrate skill self-contained: ship the R1-R15 removal table, have the CLI expose the counted issue set or the exact queries for inventory, and fix the pre-reset tag reference.

spec:
Release 1 must migrate existing users without them knowing to look for MIGRATING.md. When the CLI runs in a repository that still has pre-reset ZzzOps state, it detects that and presents migration as the next step, the way `next` presents any other action.

Detection, which must be cheap and must not break the bounded-cost rule that normal reads touch no issues or comments:
- Local and integration-branch signals, free: a schema-1 or old-format .zzzops/POLICY.json or workflow, PROJECT_AUDIT.md, BOOTSTRAP.json, old marker blocks, and old ref namespaces on the remote (for example zzzops/attempts/*, zzzops/native-candidates/*), from the fetch the CLI already does or a one-time ls-remote.
- GitHub signal, one call: open issues with the `zzzops` label or the old goal envelope marker.
- The GitHub check runs once per engine version per clone, or when the local signals fire, never on every `next`. The result is cached under the Git directory (for example .git/zzzops/), keyed by engine version, so a version change re-checks. This restores the old engine's 'version changed' detection in a bounded form. Investigate whether the old engine's equivalent was lost in the reset (R11, the installation-validation and legacy-cleanup gate) and reuse what makes sense.

Disclosure:
- When legacy state is found, `next` and `validate` report a `legacy` item, not a hard blocker, unless the policy itself is old-format, in which case it is the blocker. The item carries counts (open legacy goal issues, legacy refs, legacy files) and the exact next step.
- The next step is a shipped migrate skill (new, or MIGRATING.md promoted to a skill) that walks the agent through it: bootstrap the new policy if needed; triage the open legacy goals (close what is obsolete or delivered with a comment, recreate what still matters with `zzzops new`, linking the old issue); optionally run the cleanup tool for legacy files; and report.
- The skill follows progressive disclosure: the CLI points to it only when needed.
- Once migration is done, which is detected rather than remembered, the item disappears. Dismissal is explicit, through a policy setting such as `legacy.ignore: true` for repositories that deliberately keep old issues.

Acceptance:
- Engine tests with fake gh: a repository with legacy issues shows the legacy item once per engine version, with exactly one gh call, cached; a clean repository makes no gh call after the first check; an old-format policy is a blocker that names the migrate skill; the item disappears after migration.
- The migrate skill exists and is listed in package.py.
- The audit performed by hand on this repository (115 issues triaged on 2026-10-31) serves as the worked example in the skill.
- MIGRATING.md, CLI_USAGE, PRIVACY (if a new GitHub read is added) and SETUP are updated.
title: Detect old-style ZzzOps installations and disclose migration as the next step
